title: Write-scope hook misjudges lane commands that use shell variables or run beside another worktree
body:
On 2026-11-17 the t-g86syt0 lane (#1335) reported two PreToolUse write-scope refusals while it worked in its own worktree (.krn/worktrees/screening-verify-keeps-fields) and the lead session's cwd was another worktree (replay-session-driver):
1. a Bash command naming a path through a shell variable ($B/...) was refused as a main-checkout write: the hook does not expand variables before resolving the path.
2. while krn pr ship ran, the hook refused the lane's read-only PR polling; the scope check appeared to judge against the lead's cwd worktree rather than the lane's.
Outcome: the write-scope hook resolves variable paths it can expand (or treats unexpandable ones as unknown, not main-checkout) and judges a lane by its own worktree.
Proof: hook unit tests with a captured payload for each case (KRN-12, KRN-14).
